title: GlusterFS: decode the v4.0 procedures shown as dissect_rpc_unknown
description:
# GlusterFS: decode the v4.0 procedures previously shown as `dissect_rpc_unknown`

Closes #21366.

## What

The GlusterFS 4.0 dissector (`glusterfs4_0_fop`, RPC program 1298437 version 400) labelled 10
procedures correctly (after #21359 / !25487) but left them with no field decoder — registered as
`{ GFS3_OP_X, "X", dissect_rpc_unknown, dissect_rpc_unknown }`, so the request/reply body showed as one
opaque blob. This adds per-field decoders for **9** of them, mirroring the existing
`glusterfs_gfs4_0_op_*` style and the `rpc/xdr/src/glusterfs4-xdr.x` wire schema. **COMPOUND (49) is
intentionally left undecoded** — it was removed from GlusterFS and has no struct in `glusterfs4-xdr.x`.

| proc | name | request | reply | new code |
|------|------|---------|-------|----------|
| 37 | RCHECKSUM | `gfx_rchecksum_req` | `gfx_rchecksum_rsp` | call + reply |
| 47 | IPC | `gfx_ipc_req` | `gfx_common_rsp` | call (reuses common reply) |
| 50 | LEASE | `gfx_lease_req` | `gfx_lease_rsp` | call + reply + `gf_proto_lease` helper |
| 51 | GETACTIVELK | `gfx_getactivelk_req` | `gfx_getactivelk_rsp` | call + reply + locklist entry |
| 52 | SETACTIVELK | `gfx_setactivelk_req` | `gfx_common_rsp` | call (reuses common reply + locklist entry) |
| 53 | ICREATE | `gfx_icreate_req` | `gfx_common_iatt_rsp` | call (reuses common_iatt reply) |
| 54 | NAMELINK | `gfx_namelink_req` | `gfx_common_2iatt_rsp` | call (reuses common_2iatt reply) |
| 55 | PUT | `gfx_put_req` | `gfx_common_3iatt_rsp` | call (reuses common_3iatt reply) |
| 56 | COPY_FILE_RANGE | `gfx_copy_file_range_req` | `gfx_common_3iatt_rsp` | call (reuses common_3iatt reply) |

New shared helpers: `glusterfs_rpc_dissect_gf_proto_lease` (the 28-byte `gf_proto_lease`) and
`glusterfs_gfs4_0_locklist_entry` (one `gfs3_locklist` node), the latter walked by the existing
`dissect_rpc_list` for the `*nextentry` linked list (same pattern as `readdirp_reply`). Adds 11 `hf_`
fields and 2 `ett_` subtrees.

## How the reply structs were determined

`glusterfs4-xdr.x` defines the structs but does not bind a procedure to its reply struct; that binding is
in the GlusterFS client/server code. Each was taken from
`xlators/protocol/client/src/client-rpc-fops_v2.c` (`client4*_<op>_cbk` →
`xdr_to_generic(..., xdr_gfx_<TYPE>_rsp)`) and cross-checked against `server-rpc-fops_v2.c`
(`server4_<op>_cbk` encode side). Two cases differ from naïve expectation and are worth noting for
reviewers:

- **COPY_FILE_RANGE reply is `gfx_common_3iatt_rsp`** (stat + 2 parent iatts), not a 2-iatt reply.
- **NAMELINK reply is `gfx_common_2iatt_rsp`.**

## Verification

- **All request/reply field layouts** are `.x`-verified field-by-field (widths + XDR `opaque<>`/`string<>`
  4-byte-padding rules) and the reply-struct bindings are source-verified on both the client decode and
  server encode side.
- **Live-decoded on a GlusterFS 11.2 capture** (loopback traffic on throwaway test volumes — random GFIDs,
  no user data):
  - **COPY_FILE_RANGE (56)** — call and reply, byte-exact against issued values: `glfs_copy_file_range`
    of a known 0x100000-byte range decodes Size=1048576, off_in/off_out=0, both gfids and both fds; the
    reply's **three** IATTs (stat=source, pre/post-parent=destination) decode cleanly — empirically
    confirming the `gfx_common_3iatt_rsp` binding (not 2iatt).
  - **LEASE (50)** — call and reply: a `glfs_lease(SET, RD)` with lease_id `0x11`×16 decodes
    Command=2/Type=1/ID=`11…11`/Flags=0 (byte-exact), and the reply (ENOSYS for the anonymous gfapi
    client) exercises the new `gf_proto_lease` helper on the echoed lease. No malformed/expert items.
- **`.x`-verified only (not observed on the wire in this session):** RCHECKSUM (37), IPC (47), PUT (55),
  GETACTIVELK (51), SETACTIVELK (52), ICREATE (53), NAMELINK (54). Reasons: PUT/ICREATE/NAMELINK have no
  gfapi entry point and are internal; GET/SETACTIVELK need lock-recovery traffic; RCHECKSUM is only
  emitted by AFR data self-heal under the `diff` algorithm and did not surface in the heal-capture window;
  IPC (`glfs_ipc`) is a private API with no public opcode contract. Their structs are simple and the
  layouts are `.x`-verified; the GET/SETACTIVELK locklist walk reuses the bounded, fuzz-safe
  `dissect_rpc_list`, so the residual risk there is the per-node field layout, which is `.x`-verified.
  Flagged explicitly per the project's discipline of not claiming live verification for unobserved cases.
